title: Boss: The Leaderboard
story: The Query Hydra has four heads: a CTE, a join, a window and a filter. Cut them one by one.
goal: Make a leaderboard of delivered spend: columns name, spent and pos (1 = biggest spender, using RANK), showing only the top 3 positions (ties allowed), ordered by pos then name.
starter:
-- CTE for spend, then RANK() OVER, then filter
SELECT ;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data

hints: Step 1 CTE spend. Step 2 CTE ranked with RANK(). Step 3 join to customers and filter.
You cannot filter on a window function in the same SELECT: filter in the outer query.

WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id), ranked AS (SELECT customer_id, spent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY spent DESC) AS pos FROM spend) SELECT c.name, r.spent, r.pos FROM ranked r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id WHERE r.pos <= 3 ORDER BY r.pos, c.name;
socratic: Why a second CTE for ranking?
What would ROW_NUMBER do differently on ties?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the a CTE?
solution: WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id), ranked AS (SELECT customer_id, spent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY spent DESC) AS pos FROM spend) SELECT c.name, r.spent, r.pos FROM ranked r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id WHERE r.pos <= 3 ORDER BY r.pos, c.name;
alt: WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT name, spent, pos FROM (SELECT c.name, s.spent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.spent DESC) AS pos FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id) WHERE pos <= 3 ORDER BY pos, name;
